Edge Projection Learning Path

Understanding how three-edge-projection generates visible and hidden edges from 3D models

The Pipeline Overview

When you call ProjectionGenerator.generate(), here's what happens:

1 Generate Candidate Edges
→
2 Pre-filter Edges
→
3 Build Line BVH
→
4 BVHcast Overlaps
→
5 Convert to Lines

Each step is explained in detail in the lessons below. By the end, you'll understand exactly how the library turns a 3D mesh into clean architectural line drawings.

Lessons

01: Foundations - What Are We Drawing?

Understanding the different types of edges (hard edges, silhouette edges) and why we need them for technical drawings.

Edge Types Angle Threshold Projection Direction Visual Examples

02: Generating Candidate Edges

How EdgeGenerator collects all edges that might be visible: hard edges from face angles and silhouette edges from projection direction. (Pipeline steps 1-2)

Vertex Hashing Edge Matching Normal Comparison generateEdges.js

03: Intersection Edges (Optional)

Detecting edges where two triangles penetrate each other. Not needed for most use cases - can be disabled with includeIntersectionEdges = false.

Triangle-Triangle Intersection BVH Acceleration Optional Feature

04: Occlusion & Clipping - BVHcast Overlaps

Building a BVH of all lines, then comparing against mesh BVHs to find which sections are occluded. The core visibility algorithm. (Pipeline steps 3-4)

LineObjectsBVH bvhcastEdges Overlap Ranges Range Merging

05: Converting Overlaps to Lines

How overlap ranges are converted to visible/hidden line segments, and how ProjectionGenerator orchestrates the full pipeline. (Pipeline step 5)
